_README: External survey for the #269 KG gap analysis. `fetched:true` means the page body was actually retrieved in this lane (by the lane conductor or a lane researcher); `fetched:false` means the claim rests on a search-result snippet only and is NOT a verified reading of the source. Claims are separated into what a system DEMONSTRABLY carries as a content/data type vs what an author RECOMMENDS. `our_status` names which of our existing node families (component / pattern / context / token / ruling / guideline / principle / sc / axe / role / session / artefact / evidence) the thing lands in, if any.

node_families: role — SLOT role, i.e. provides/wants (roles.json, 12 roles)
ours_for_reference.note: roles.json is explicitly a SLOT-role vocabulary ('the thing a slot asks for'), NOT an end-user persona vocabulary. That distinction drives gap G-07.

sources.title: W3C DTCG — Design Tokens Format Module (Editor's Draft)
sources.what_it_models: A token = name + $value + $type, organised into arbitrary $groups, with aliases/references, $description, $deprecated, $extensions (vendor namespaced), 8 base types (color, dimension, fontFamily, fontWeight, duration, cubicBezier, number, +additional) and composite types (strokeStyle, border, transition, shadow, gradient, typography).

sources.title: Figma — Modes for variables
sources.what_it_models: A variable collection carries N MODES (one value per variable per mode); modes are the declared mechanism for theme, accessible/high-contrast themes, LOCALISED UI COPY (string variables) and device size. Objects/pages resolve mode by inheritance ('Auto') up the layer tree, with an explicit default mode and documented MODE-CONFLICT failure when versions fan out across files. Imports DTCG JSON; cross-collection aliasing via com.figma.aliasData.

sources.title: Figma — Code Connect (React reference)
sources.what_it_models: An explicit typed binding between a Figma component/variant and a code component, including per-prop mapping (string/boolean/enum/instance/children/nestedProps/className/slot) and variant restrictions that select a different code component per variant combination.

sources.title: Supernova — SDK data model (Token)
sources.what_it_models: Design system as versioned objects: Workspace / Brand / DesignSystemVersion / Theme, with Token (id, brandId, themeId, designSystemVersionId, tokenType, origin, parentGroupId, propertyValues), token groups, Components, Custom/Element Properties, Assets and Pipelines.

sources.title: zeroheight — documentation product
sources.what_it_models: A doc layer over Figma/Storybook: styleguide, versioned pages, components carrying an explicit STATUS (released / in progress / needs attention) split across design, code and docs, tokens synced from Figma variables, integrations and roles. 'Adoption insights' / ROI is vendor positioning, not a documented schema.

sources.title: Knapsack — docs
sources.what_it_models: 'Design system as data': code sources + design (Figma) sources, Patterns composed of components with status, Design tokens with Collections/Groups/MODES, pages built from typed content blocks, demos/prototypes that instantiate real components, and an MCP server + llms.txt that exposes all of it to AI tools.

sources.title: Storybook — Accessibility testing
sources.what_it_models: Component → meta → story (args/parameters/decorators/play), with the a11y addon running axe-core RULES against each story and attaching Violations / Passes / Incomplete plus a per-story test status. Rules are enable/disable/selector-scoped per story.

sources.title: GOV.UK Design System — Patterns
sources.what_it_models: A three-tier split (Styles / Components / Patterns) where a Pattern is a 'best practice design solution for specific user-focused tasks and page types', explicitly grouped by INTENT ('Ask users for…', 'Help users to…', 'Pages'), and where patterns 'often use one or more components and explain how to adapt them to the context'. Includes bank-details and payment-card-details patterns.

sources.title: GOV.UK Design System — home / community backlog
sources.what_it_models: A public backlog where a candidate component/pattern must carry documented RESEARCH (who it was tested with, in what context) before promotion, plus lifecycle statuses (e.g. Experimental/Trial → Stable) and versioned release notes. (Backlog research requirement read via its GitHub doc by the lane researcher; treat the exact promotion wording as reported, not quoted.)

sources.title: IBM Carbon Design System
sources.what_it_models: Splits ELEMENTS (color, type, spacing, icons, PICTOGRAMS, motion, grid) from GUIDELINES (content, accessibility, motion usage) from COMPONENTS and PATTERNS ('harvested from products'), each with a named maintainer, plus a separate data-visualisation/Carbon Charts token family.

sources.title: Atlassian Design System
sources.what_it_models: Foundations (Color, Typography, Iconography, Grid, Accessibility) separate from Components, with flat namespaced tokens (color.text.accent.red, elevation.surface.hovered) and distinct content/voice-and-tone and illustration tracks reachable from nav (those specific pages NOT fetched).

sources.title: U.S. Web Design System — components overview
sources.what_it_models: Separates Components / Patterns / Templates / Design tokens / Utilities, and — the distinctive bit — publishes a per-component ACCESSIBILITY TESTS subpage enumerating criterion-level tests (e.g. Modal ~14 tests, Search ~22), i.e. test evidence attached to the component node.

sources.title: Material 3 — design tokens / type / motion / shape
sources.what_it_models: Three-tier tokens (reference → system → component), colour ROLES with on-X pairs, a 15-cell type scale (5 roles × 3 sizes), motion as easing+duration token pairs, a shape scale, state layers, and window size classes for adaptive layout. NOT FETCHED: the m3.material.io page returned empty (JS-rendered); claims rest on search snippets and the Material Symbols axes page below.

sources.title: Material Symbols — variable icon axes
sources.what_it_models: Icons as a variable font with four typed axes — weight (100–700), fill (0/1), grade (−50–200), optical size (20–48) — so a glyph is a point in an axis space, not a file. Snippet only.

sources.title: Salesforce Lightning Design System
sources.what_it_models: Two-tier: framework-independent BLUEPRINT (semantic HTML/CSS + a11y attributes + guidelines) vs framework-specific Component that implements it, joined by design tokens / styling hooks. NO end-user persona entity was found. Snippet only (site is a JS shell).

sources.title: Microsoft Fluent 2
sources.what_it_models: Icons as a first-class family with filled/outline pairs and literal-metaphor naming, illustration as a separate track, motion patterns anchored to the spatial origin of the invoking action, and advisory notes on cultural connotation of icons for localisation. Snippet only.

sources.title: Adobe Spectrum
sources.what_it_models: PLATFORM SCALE (desktop vs mobile) as a first-class sizing axis a component branches on, rem-based typography that scales with user preference, international design guidance (RTL mirroring, locale-aware date/currency/number formatting), and per-component content standards. Snippet only.

sources.title: Shopify Polaris — content
sources.what_it_models: NOTE: this URL now 302-redirects to https://shopify.dev/docs/api/polaris, a component/API reference for Polaris web components across app surfaces (App Home, Admin, Checkout, Customer accounts, POS) — i.e. SURFACE is a first-class axis. The former standalone content-guidelines section was not served at this URL when fetched; content-rule claims below are snippet-level only.

sources.title: Shopify Polaris — product content guidelines
sources.what_it_models: Content rules by category (grammar, naming, inclusive language) with example + rationale, and an explicit reading-level target. Snippet only.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group — tone-of-voice dimensions
sources.what_it_models: AUTHOR RECOMMENDATION, not a shipped system: tone as four measurable dimensions (funny↔serious, formal↔casual, respectful↔irreverent, enthusiastic↔matter-of-fact), each a scale position. Snippet only.

sources.title: Home Office Design System — readability
sources.what_it_models: A target reading age (9) as a governing standard on content, with literacy-statistics rationale. Snippet only.

sources.title: digital.gov — Federal Plain Language Guidelines
sources.what_it_models: Plain-language techniques grouped by audience analysis / organisation / word choice / testing, with a statutory basis (Plain Writing Act 2010). Snippet only.

sources.title: IPTC Photo Metadata Standard
sources.what_it_models: The image-asset record: Headline/Description/Keywords, Creator/CopyrightNotice/DateCreated, a rights block (usageTerms, licensor, webStatementOfRights), PersonShown/ProductShown depiction, ImageRegion (focal/crop), and 2025.1 AI-generation fields (AIPromptInformation, AISystemUsed). Snippet only.

sources.title: Frontify — metadata and tags guide
sources.what_it_models: VENDOR GUIDANCE: brand-asset records with usage rights, expiration date, market restriction, product line and controlled-vocabulary tags (incl. mood), surfaced through audience-scoped portals. Snippet only.

sources.title: IBM Carbon — pictograms contribution guidance
sources.what_it_models: Pictogram grammar: 32×32 grid, padding in grid units, stroke spec, keyline optical alignment, productive vs expressive families. Snippet only.

sources.title: W3C — Understanding WCAG 2.2
sources.what_it_models: The normative four-layer structure: Principle (4) → Guideline (13) → Success Criterion (numbered, level A/AA/AAA) → Techniques, where techniques are typed as SUFFICIENT, ADVISORY or FAILURE. Snippet only.

sources.title: W3C — ACT Rules Format
sources.what_it_models: A rule schema: applicability + expectation + accessibility requirement (primary conformance / secondary), so a rule is formally tied to the SC it tests. Snippet only.

sources.title: axe-core — rule development doc
sources.what_it_models: Rule metadata fields: id, description, help, impact (minor/moderate/serious/critical), tags (wcag###, best-practice, act, section508), and pass/fail/incomplete messages. Snippet only.

sources.title: User Interviews — atomic UX research nuggets
sources.what_it_models: AUTHOR/COMMUNITY MODEL (Daniel Pidcock), not a shipped system: Experiment → Fact (no assumption) → Insight (synthesis of facts) → Recommendation (evidenced by insights), as reusable, addressable research atoms. Snippet only.

sources.title: Into Design Systems — Agentic Design Systems guide
sources.what_it_models: AUTHOR POSITION (2026): an 'agentic design system' is infrastructure that lets AI agents read and reason over components, tokens and guidelines autonomously; cites WhatsApp, GitHub, Indeed, New York State as examples. Snippet only — treat as framing, not evidence.

sources.title: Harness — why Harness AI uses a knowledge graph
sources.what_it_models: VENDOR CLAIM: a schema-driven knowledge graph makes agent queries deterministic and cuts token cost 15–25× vs raw MCP API crawling. Relevant as an argument for a typed graph over prose retrieval; the multiplier is unverified. Snippet only.

gap_ranking.gap: G-01 Content standard as a typed node (tone dimensions, reading level, error-message rule) with a component/surface edge
gap_ranking.why: A super-designer writes the words. Polaris, Carbon, Atlassian and GOV.UK all carry content as a first-class track; ours exists only as prose guidelines, so no gate can test a sentence the way _validate_* tests a pixel. Banking copy is also the highest-risk output we produce.

gap_ranking.gap: G-02 End-user persona / job-to-be-done node, distinct from our slot-role vocabulary
gap_ranking.why: GOV.UK organises its entire pattern library by user task ('Ask users for…', 'Help users to…'). We index by UI shape and by context. Without a user-intent node the agent cannot answer 'what should this screen be' — only 'what could go on it'.

gap_ranking.gap: G-03 Mode axis (theme / density / contrast / locale / size) as a node with defaults and inheritance
gap_ranking.why: Figma's variable modes and Knapsack's token modes make this the load-bearing abstraction. We have four themes plus light/dark handled as parallel token sets, which is the fan-out that Figma's own docs describe as producing mode conflicts.

gap_ranking.gap: G-04 Lifecycle status + owner per node
gap_ranking.why: zeroheight, Knapsack, GOV.UK and Carbon all carry it; it is what tells the agent whether it may reach for a thing and who to ask. Cheap to add (one field + one edge) and it makes every other gate more honest.

gap_ranking.gap: G-05 Evidence chain: user-research finding → evidence → recommendation, and per-component accessibility test RESULTS as nodes
gap_ranking.why: USWDS publishes criterion-level test evidence per component; GOV.UK gates promotion on documented research. Our ruling chain is excellent for OUR decisions and silent about the user. For a CAIO demo this is the difference between a library and a defensible system.
Figma Code Connect shows the granularity actually needed to emit correct code per variant. We bind at component level, so the agent's variant choice does not survive into the snippet.

gap_ranking.gap: G-07 Locale / script / direction node with font fallback and format rules
gap_ranking.why: Spectrum and Fluent both carry it; Figma models localised copy as a MODE. Multi-locale banking is a near-term requirement and RTL mirroring changes layout decisions, not just strings.

gap_ranking.gap: G-08 WCAG technique/FAILURE layer under the success criterion
gap_ranking.why: WCAG's own structure is principle → guideline → SC → sufficient/advisory/FAILURE. Our rules are flat against the SC. The failure techniques are the negative knowledge an agent most needs and we do not carry the type.

gap_ranking.gap: G-09 Brand/imagery asset as a node with rights, expiry, market, mood, focal point and depiction
gap_ranking.why: IPTC and every DAM carry it; we already have the licence fields in _PHOTOGRAPHY-MANIFEST.json, so this is a promotion of existing data into the graph rather than new research. Expiry and market restriction are the fields that prevent a legal incident.

gap_ranking.gap: G-10 Icon/pictogram axis model and the outlined↔filled pair edge
gap_ranking.why: Material Symbols treats a glyph as a point in a weight/fill/grade/optical-size space. Our #264 -active glyph twins ARE that pair relation, built by hand and unmodelled — the gap is already costing us.

gap_ranking.gap: G-11 Deprecation with a machine-readable replacement
gap_ranking.why: DTCG's $deprecated explicitly anticipates a tool resolving the replacement and linking to the new token. We rename via aliasOf and lose the reason and the migration path.

gap_ranking.gap: G-12 Motion pattern node (easing+duration pair, spatial origin, reduced-motion fallback)
gap_ranking.why: Carbon's productive/expressive split and Fluent's 'anchored to the point of invocation' are meaning, not values. Lower weight only because our current demo surface is largely static.

gap_ranking.gap: G-13 Template / page-type as a node family
gap_ranking.why: USWDS and GOV.UK both carry whole-page types. Ours exist as sources inside context nodes, which works today; promoting them is tidying, not capability.

gap_ranking.gap: G-14 Surface node constraining the legal component set
gap_ranking.why: Polaris exposes different component sets per surface (Admin / Checkout / POS). We have one surface, so this is a shape to leave room for rather than build.

gap_ranking.gap: G-15 Serving the graph to agents (MCP / llms.txt)
gap_ranking.why: Knapsack ships an MCP server over exactly this data. It is a distribution question, not a model question — but it is the thing that turns the graph from our tool into the product's.

cautions: DTCG explicitly warns that groups are arbitrary and 'tools SHOULD NOT use them to infer the type or purpose of design tokens' (fetched). Do not let a folder path become a semantic edge — several of our existing prose-derived edges are close to this failure already.

Figma's own mode documentation devotes a long section to MODE CONFLICTS and a four-file publish-in-order recovery procedure. Every mode axis multiplies the surface that must be republished in step. Add modes as an axis only where a real decision branches on it; do not mint a mode per theme-per-density-per-locale.

Vendor 'design system health', 'adoption insights' and 'ROI' framing (zeroheight, Supernova, Knapsack, Harness) is POSITIONING, not schema. The lane researchers could not find documented field definitions behind any of it. Do not copy a metric node whose definition is a marketing page.

Salesforce's blueprint-vs-component split duplicates the same knowledge twice (spec + implementation) and SLDS2 is reportedly re-prioritising CSS custom properties over the SLDS1 token layer — i.e. the two-tier model needed a migration. A second parallel representation of a component is a maintenance bill, and we already pay one (meta + snippet).

The atomic-research nugget model (Fact → Insight → Recommendation) is an AUTHOR/COMMUNITY model, not a shipped system, and its known failure mode in practice is nuggets accumulating faster than anyone re-reads them. If we adopt it, adopt the CHAIN (three typed nodes) and not the aspiration of decomposing every study.

Six separate domains here (research, WCAG, axe, content, tone, rights) each model the same underlying shape: a claim with a typed support link back to something that justifies it. Resist building six bespoke schemas. One evidence/justification edge with a typed kind is likely to survive maintenance where six will not — but this is a lane RECOMMENDATION, not something any source states.

Persona taxonomies are the classic design-system ontology that collapses: nobody updates them and they drift from the research. If G-02 is adopted, bind persona/job nodes to an evidence node (G-05) so an unsupported persona is visibly unsupported, rather than letting them stand as free assertions.

Several claims in this file are snippet-level only — Material 3, SLDS, Fluent, Spectrum, Polaris content, IPTC, NNG, atomic research, axe rule doc, WCAG Understanding. The m3.material.io page returned EMPTY on fetch (JS-rendered), and https://polaris.shopify.com/content now 302-redirects to shopify.dev's API reference. Do not quote any of these as verified until re-fetched, ideally with a headless browser (knowledge/_render/seat_env.sh).
